source.title: Do VLAs Know They Will Fail? Interpretable Success and Failure Patterns in Physical AI Systems
source.authors: Christian A. Rogers; Qian Lin; Daniel S. Brown

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses held-out detection scoring to validate behavioral descriptions of SAE features, a method related to automated explanation scoring. It does not test the claim's neuron-level results or any listed version.
record.gate_note: The paper studies OpenVLA SAE features, not neuron poles or language-model neuron explanations. Its held-out video-clip scoring is related to automated explanation scoring but does not measure the neuron behavior or system named in any claim version. No claim version is tested. The paper also reports outcome prediction and feature–task associations, but those results do not test the listed neuron claims.
record.test_reason: The study trains a TopK SAE on OpenVLA-7B layer-0 activations. It validates VLM-written descriptions of selected SAE features by detection scoring on held-out video clips. It uses explanation scoring as a tool for its own pipeline. It does not score neuron explanations in a language model on new text, so it does not measure what V7 names. It also does not measure neuron-pole shares (V1, V2), revisit InceptionV1 (V3), vary architecture or tools (V4), build neuron attribution graphs (V5), or test activating-example explanations of neurons (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE features keep OpenVLA's outcome-predictive information and allow failure warning before an estimated point of no return. They also conclude that VLM descriptions of outcome-associated features are validated in aggregate on held-out clips, with individual descriptions treated as hypotheses.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses a TopK SAE on VLA residual-stream activations, selects outcome-associated features, and evaluates VLM-generated behavioral descriptions on held-out video clips; it does not use the neuron-explanation procedure described in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Description specificity varied across feature–task pairs; the paper reports the feature-850 description was anti-correlated with its activation and that some transport descriptions were not specific.

fits_no_version.finding: VLM descriptions of 12 selected OpenVLA SAE feature–task pairs scored a mean held-out detection AUROC of 0.76, versus 0.58 for shuffled descriptions. Pairs varied: feature 850 scored 0.42, and several transport descriptions were not specific.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Detection-scored descriptions of selected VLA SAE features predict held-out activation on average, but are uneven per feature.

fits_no_version.finding: The mean Spearman correlation between description-based clip scores and feature activation was 0.46.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Description-based scores for VLA SAE features correlate moderately with activation.

record.problems: The paper reports only 24 clips per feature–task pair, and says an individual AUROC has a confidence interval of roughly ±0.2. Description specificity varies; one description is anti-correlated with activation. The study concerns VLA SAE features and held-out video clips, so it does not establish the listed language-model neuron claims.
record.rows_left_out: No additional findings were left out.

untested.parts: All: neuron interpretability shares across language models and scales.
All: InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.

All: neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
All: whether activating-example explanations of neurons predict firing.

record.verdict_notes: The study cites Bills et al. (an original source) only as a scoring method. Its 'features' are SAE directions in a vision-language-action model, not neurons in a language model, so no version applies.

The InceptionV1 cat-and-car example and the proposed shared-pose interpretation.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality, and the stated vision-model estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons and reconstruction error.
Neuron explanations based on activating examples and prediction of neuron firing.
Automated scores for neuron explanations on new text, including the stated minority-good-score result.

conditions.value: judge VLM sees only the description

rows.measure: Mean AUROC for descriptions predicting feature activation
rows.note: This is an aggregate over 12 feature–task pairs, not neuron explanations or new text. The paper also reports that descriptions outperform shuffled descriptions on 11 of 12 pairs; mean ΔAUROC = 0.17, 95% CI over clips [0.10, 0.24], sign test p = 0.003. Resampling pairs as well widens that interval to [−0.01, 0.35].
rows.check: Linkage correct. This is SAE-feature description scoring in a VLA on video clips, not neuron explanations simulated on text. Aggregate over 12 hand-selected outcome-associated feature–task pairs.
